import pytest
from isort.wrap import import_statement, Config

# Existing test cases
def test_import_statement_basic():
    result = import_statement('import module', ['dependency'])
    assert result == 'import module\n    from dependency';  # Expected behavior depending on the formatter

def test_import_statement_with_comments():
    result = import_statement('import module', ['dependency'], comments=['This is a comment'])
    assert 'This is a comment' in result

def test_import_statement_multiline():
    config = Config(wrap_length=20)
    result = import_statement('import very_long_module_name', ['dep1', 'dep2'], config=config)
    assert result.count('\n') > 1  # Expect more than one line for long imports

def test_import_statement_explode():
    result = import_statement('import module', ['dependency'], explode=True)
    assert result == 'import module,\n    from dependency'  # Validate results with explosion

@pytest.mark.parametrize('line_separator', ['\n', ';'])
def test_import_statement_line_separator(line_separator):
    result = import_statement('import module', ['dependency'], line_separator=line_separator)
    assert line_separator in result  # Ensure the line separator affects output.

    config = Config(balanced_wrapping=True)
    result = import_statement('import module', ['dep1', 'dep2'], config=config)
    assert result.count('\n') > 1  # Ensure that balanced wrapping is applied correctly

def test_import_statement_no_imports():
    result = import_statement('import module', [], comments=[])
    assert 'import module' in result  # Ensure the function can handle no imports gracefully

    assert result == ''  # Check behavior with an empty import statement
